youtube_video.title: What Is Zoho One? How It Works, What's Included and Who It Suits
youtube_video.description:
Read the full guide: https://zudoworks.com/insights/what-is-zoho-one/

Zoho One is often described as "Zoho's version of Microsoft 365" or "everything Zoho makes". Neither is quite right. It is a licensing and administration layer: one subscription that switches on more than 45 Zoho business apps for the people you choose, with one sign-in, one admin panel and one invoice. This explainer covers how it works, the two ways to pay, what sits outside the suite, a note for buyers in Australia, New Zealand and the UK, and who it suits. Everything was checked on Zoho's own pages on 28 November 2026. We do not quote prices: Zoho shows them on its own pricing page in your local currency.

Chapters
00:00 What is Zoho One?
00:05 One sign-in, one admin panel, one invoice
00:09 Assign only the apps each person needs
00:13 All Employee pricing
00:19 Flexible User pricing
00:24 What is not included
00:30 Payroll in Australia, New Zealand and the UK
00:35 Who Zoho One suits
00:39 Read the full guide

Key facts
- Zoho One is one subscription for more than 45 Zoho apps, including CRM, Books, Desk, People, Inventory, Mail, Projects, Creator and Analytics. The apps are the same ones Zoho sells on their own, not cut-down versions.
- The admin panel is Zoho Directory: add a person once, put them in a group, and assign only the apps they need. Users sign in once and see their apps.
- All Employee Pricing licenses everyone on payroll at a lower rate per person. Flexible User Pricing licenses only the people you choose, at a higher rate per user. Neither has a minimum number of users.
- Not included, according to Zoho's FAQ: Zoho ERP, Catalyst, FSM, Shifts, RouteIQ, paid Marketplace extensions and domain registration, among others.
- Zoho Payroll is offered in Zoho One only in nine other countries, so businesses in Australia, New Zealand and the UK need a separate payroll product connected to Zoho People and Zoho Books.
- It suits a business that will use four or more Zoho apps across several teams. For one or two apps, buying them on their own is usually simpler.
- Every account can start with Zoho's 30-day free trial, which needs no card.

Zudo Works builds on Zoho for growing businesses in the UK, the US, Australia and New Zealand. More guides: https://zudoworks.com/insights/

linkedin_profile_video:
The question I hear most from owners weighing up Zoho is a simple one: what do I actually get with Zoho One?

The honest answer is a licence, not a product. One subscription switches on more than 45 Zoho apps for the people you choose. You get one sign-in, one admin panel and one bill. What you then do with those apps is where the work, and the value, sit.

Three things I make sure every buyer understands before they sign:

How you pay. All Employee Pricing means a licence for everyone on payroll, at a lower rate. Flexible User Pricing means only the people you pick, at a higher rate. If most of your staff will use at least one app, the first usually makes sense. If only a few will, it often doesn't.

What is outside it. Zoho ERP, Catalyst and FSM are separate products. Manufacturers in particular assume Zoho ERP is in the bundle. It isn't.

Payroll. In Australia, New Zealand and the UK, Zoho Payroll is not part of Zoho One. Plan a separate payroll product and connect it to Zoho People and Books.

My rule of thumb: four or more apps across at least two teams, and Zoho One is worth a serious look. One or two apps, and you are usually better buying them on their own.

I have put the full breakdown, with Zoho's own sources, here: https://zudoworks.com/insights/what-is-zoho-one/

Before any client signs up for Zoho One, I ask them to count two things: the apps they will really use, and the people who will really log in.

Those two numbers decide almost everything.

Four or more apps across several teams, and the suite usually pays for itself. One or two apps, and buying them on their own is simpler.

Most of your staff in at least one app, and All Employee Pricing tends to make sense. Only a handful, and Flexible User Pricing or individual apps are often the better buy.
